lessons.title: Counter App — Typed
objectives: Define a functional component with an explicit JSX.Element return type and typed props (avoid React.FC)
Declare state with an explicit type parameter via `useState<number>`
Type event handlers as `() => void` and wire them to `onClick` props

lessons.title: Toggle Visibility — Typed
objectives: Implement a boolean state variable using `useState<boolean>` to control visibility
Conditionally render JSX using a ternary operator and the state variable
Type a toggle function as `() => void` and bind it to a button’s `onClick`

lessons.title: Controlled Input — Typed
objectives: Create a controlled input using `useState<string>` and the `value`/`onChange` pattern
Type the `onChange` handler as `(e: React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => void`
Validate input length and update state only if constraints are met

lessons.title: Multiple State Variables — Typed
objectives: Declare and manage multiple state variables with explicit types (e.g., `useState<string>`, `useState<number>`)
Update state variables independently using setters with correct type inference
Log state changes to the console using a `useEffect` with dependency array

lessons.title: Conditional Rendering with Ternary — Typed
objectives: Render JSX conditionally using a ternary operator and a boolean state variable
Type a component’s props to accept optional children with `React.ReactNode`
Use a discriminated union to type props for mutually exclusive render states

lessons.title: List Rendering with map() — Typed
objectives: Iterate over an array of objects using `map()` and render a list of components
Type the array and its elements using an interface (e.g., `Array<{ id: number; name: string }>`)
Assign a unique `key` prop to each list item using an object property

lessons.title: useEffect & Side Effects — Typed
objectives: Fetch data in a `useEffect` hook and type the response using an interface
Manage loading and error states with `useState<boolean>` and `useState<string | null>`
Clean up side effects using a return function in `useEffect`

lessons.title: Forms & Validation — Typed
objectives: Build a form with controlled inputs and type each field’s state and handler
Validate form data using a custom function and display errors conditionally
Submit form data and type the submission handler as `(e: React.FormEvent) => void`

lessons.title: Color Picker — Typed
objectives: Implement a color picker using `useState<string>` and an `<input type='color'>`
Type the color change handler as `(e: React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => void`
Apply the selected color to a `<div>`’s inline style using template literals

lessons.title: Reusable Button — Typed
objectives: Create a reusable button component with typed props for `onClick`, `disabled`, and `variant`
Use `React.ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement>` to extend native button props
Apply conditional styling based on the `variant` prop using a TypeScript union

lessons.title: Card Component — Typed
objectives: Design a card component with typed props for `title`, `description`, and `footer`
Use `React.ReactNode` to type slots for flexible content insertion
Style the card using CSS Modules and type the class names as `string`

lessons.title: Props Drilling — Typed
objectives: Pass data from a parent to a deeply nested child via intermediate components
Type each prop explicitly at every level of the component hierarchy
Refactor to use Context API to avoid props drilling, typing the context value

lessons.title: Default Props — Typed
objectives: Define default props for a component using `DefaultFunctionProps<T>` or inline defaults
Type optional props using `?` and provide fallback values in the function signature
Use destructuring with default values in the component parameters

lessons.title: Children Prop — Typed
objectives: Create a wrapper component that accepts and renders `children` of type `React.ReactNode`
Type the component’s props to explicitly include `children`
Apply consistent styling to all children using `React.Children.map`

lessons.title: TypeScript Interface for Props — Typed
objectives: Replace `PropTypes` with a TypeScript interface for component props
Use union types to restrict prop values to a specific set (e.g., `'primary' | 'secondary'`)
Extend an interface to create variants of a component with shared props

lessons.title: Component Composition — Typed
objectives: Compose multiple components to build a complex UI (e.g., a modal with header, body, footer)
Type each sub-component’s props and use `React.ReactNode` for content slots
Pass handlers and state between composed components using typed callbacks

lessons.title: Custom Hook: useFetch — Typed
objectives: Write a `useFetch<T>` hook that accepts a URL and returns typed data, loading, and error states
Use generics to type the API response (e.g., `useFetch<User[]>`)
Implement error handling and retry logic with typed error messages

lessons.title: Custom Hook: useToggle — Typed
objectives: Create a `useToggle` hook that manages a boolean state and returns typed toggler functions
Type the return value as `[boolean, { toggle: () => void; setOn: () => void; setOff: () => void }]`
Use the hook in a component to toggle visibility or feature flags

lessons.title: Generic useFetch<T> — Typed
objectives: Refactor `useFetch` to use generics for flexible response typing (e.g., `useFetch<TData>`)
Type the hook’s options parameter to include headers, method, and body
Handle different response shapes (e.g., paginated data, single object) using generics

lessons.title: Discriminated Union Props — Typed
objectives: Type component props using a discriminated union for mutually exclusive states
Use a `kind` property to discriminate between variants (e.g., `{ kind: 'loading' } | { kind: 'success'; data: T }`)
Render UI conditionally based on the discriminated prop

lessons.title: useRef Typing — Typed
objectives: Create a ref for a DOM element using `useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)`
Type a ref for mutable values using `useRef<number>` and update it without re-renders
Access and manipulate the DOM element’s properties using the typed ref

lessons.title: Form Library from Scratch — Typed
objectives: Design a custom form library with typed hooks for `useForm`, `useField`, and validation
Type form values, errors, and touch states using generics (e.g., `UseFormReturn<TValues>`)
Integrate the library with a UI component and handle submission with full type safety
